change: Shared fan-in accepts an optional allocation budget for scheduler directory and per-task bookkeeping. Task slots are admitted before launch, remain charged through asynchronous boundary/reduction, and release after reduction or drained failure. Window and aggregate Parquet task paths forward caller budgets. Generic undefined inputs/partials are processed instead of hanging or silently disappearing.

edgeCases: exact scheduler peak success and peak minus one rejection
admission failure drains a blocked sibling while its charge remains live
undefined input and partial reach reducer
run, boundary and reducer failures preserve first error and drain siblings

concurrentOwnedWindowFixture.transport: memoryStore-backed real Parquet; not remote HTTP or Cloudflare
assertions: all four jobs hold partials concurrently at an async boundary
pool rejects a competing request above available capacity
all final window ordinals and representative payload match
releasing one result lowers reservations while siblings remain charged
releasing all outputs returns shared reservations to zero
peak reservations never exceed pool cap

limits: Scheduler charges are explicit accounting units, not measurements of VM promise or closure heap size.
Task output and accumulator payloads retain their independent ownership requirements.
SQL metadata fan-in has no forwarded allocation budget yet.
Concurrent 64/128 MiB acceptance and production Worker total-memory bounds remain open.

Aggregate accumulator lifecycle audit: createVectorAggregateStates accepts an optional creation scope only, but Parquet aggregate-task calls do not supply it; update/restore/merge state mainly uses QueryBudget logical limits rather than shared allocation ownership. Scheduler admission does not establish aggregate accumulator bounds.
